title: Reality Fracture Common + Uncommon Set Review
scale: Letter grades A+ through F; C+ means nearly uncuttable in its colors, C is good filler or an archetype pillar, D+ is under-supported synergy, F is never playable. Sideboard-only cards get a separate sideboard grade.

format.summary: A complex, balanced set built around Empower Jace, which creates or loads a Jace planeswalker token with -1 surveil 1 and -3 draw a card. Ten archetypes: five allied 'school' pairs on rails with hybrid prepared spells, and five broader enemy pairs for experienced drafters. Packs have fewer commons (71 in set) plus three mirrored/echo-pair legends, so decks are uncommon- and rare-heavy with high average power. Play skill and deckbuilding matter a lot, so stats may diverge between top players and all players.
format.speed: Likely midrange to grindy rather than fast. Red lacks aggressive two-drops and the RB ping plan looks weak, but you need early creatures, ideally 2-power or evasive, to pressure opposing Jace tokens and protect your own.

colors.take: Possibly the best color at common and uncommon, with strong card advantage, surveil enablers, Countersculpt, and Unsummon.
Strong uncommons, solid commons, and great ramp payoffs; no broken commons.

Called the second-worst color, with good removal but lacking the usual busted rares at lower rarity.

pairs.take: Aggro-tempo flyers built around surveil; possibly one of the strongest because its cards all pull the same way.

Pinging for non-combat damage; the most dubious archetype, probably better built grindy around Command the Stage than as burn-aggro.
Ramp and artifacts via Heartwood tokens, deliberately easy to play; Craftwork Crusher is a premium payoff, and it can also build aggressively with charms.
Lifegain and +1/+1 counters; looks pushed and scary, though lifegain payoffs are fewer than they appear.
Attrition, sacrifice, and counters; Twisted Fates is a standout.
A broad spells/prowess deck; Clash of Elements and Twinned Vision are glue.
Graveyard midrange with Hapatra; the advertised deathtouch-plus-trample theme looks thin.
Counters-matter with haste enablers like Mabel and Gallia.
Wants maximum Empower Jace and multiple Way enchantments; Kiora's 8/8 plan is a trap.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: A great balancing knob: Empower 3 is about a card, Empower 2 about two-thirds. You can activate Jace only once per turn, so empowering again only gives a second activation if the first one used up all the loyalty; even numbers like 2 and 4 create interesting tension.

mechanics.name: Prepared
mechanics.take: Each school's common/uncommon hybrid prepared spell is unique to that pair. The GW spell is closest to worth its cost, while the UB and RB one-mana spells don't affect the board. You've seen every copy of each once you've seen the multicolor section, so don't overestimate their density.

mechanics.name: Way enchantments
mechanics.take: Legendary enchantments that empower Jace and grant new walker abilities or triggers; they linger and make every later empower threatening. Way of the Healer is the best; Necromancer and Mentor are the worst.

mechanics.name: Echo/mirrored pairs
mechanics.take: Three per pack: one full pair plus half of another, often rares. Seeing which pair is missing lets you infer what the drafter who passed you likely took.

mechanics.name: Threshold
mechanics.take: Seven or more cards in the graveyard; it rewards stats on commons but lacks keywords, and can be turned on at instant speed with the charm and mill.

mechanics.name: Planeswalker dual lands
mechanics.take: Ten tapped duals that enter untapped if you control a planeswalker, graded C+; two-mana fixing lands are no longer needed.

mechanics.name: Basic landcycling
mechanics.take: Two-mana landcyclers with mana value 6 fetch any basic and are good reanimation and Hapatra enablers; costly to use on turn two in this format.

mechanics.name: Color-hate cycle
mechanics.take: Efficient sideboard cards hitting two colors.

advice: When attacking a Jace token, send one awkward-to-block creature at it and the rest at the opponent's face; don't overcommit damage to a low-loyalty Jace.
Attacking down a Jace is effectively like gaining life, so pressure it, but prioritize face when the opponent is low.
Prioritize strong uncommons and rares: roughly half of each draft's cards are commons, so decks are high-powered.
Draft early two-drops that can attack to pressure opposing Jace tokens.
In enemy pairs, draft good stuff first and lean into synergies only as they appear.
Triple-pipped gold uncommons are meant for their pair, so don't expect to splash them easily.
Unsummon is premium in a format full of big tokens.
Use Campus Crier's graveyard ability after the opponent kills your Jace rather than to protect it.
Don't attack with Surveillance Phantasm while tapped out into green reach or white flying tricks.
When an opponent targets your token with Clash of Elements, choose not to put it on top and take the two damage.
Play at most one Medic's Kitesail.
